name: Carpets, handicrafts and artisan workshops
shape_facts: Product type (carpets/rugs, textiles, wood, metal, onyx/stone, pottery, embroidery, mixed).
Workshop-based, home-based artisans through contractors, or a mix.
Number of artisans/looms working for them.
Sales: export buyers, local showrooms, exhibitions, tourists, online (Etsy, Instagram, own site).
Who supplies raw materials (wool, dyes, wood, thread) — owner or artisan.
Payment to artisans: piece rate, advance, or per square foot/knot.
scope_rule: pi notes business problems: artisan work-in-progress, advances, raw materials, order timelines, quality consistency, export admin effort, online sales, pricing and cash. It gives no labour-law, child-labour, export-regulation, customs, intellectual-property or authentication advice. It records no names, IDs or home locations of artisans, only roles and counts. If anyone is in danger or a child is being harmed, pi stops and points to emergency services and appropriate child-protection helplines.

vocabulary.knot count / KPSI: knots per square inch, quality measure
vocabulary.washing / finishing: final wash and clipping of carpets

artisans and wip: Roughly how many artisans or looms work for you?
How do you know what each is working on?
How often do you get updates?
advances: How do you match them against finished work?
materials: Who buys the wool, thread or wood?
How is what’s given out tracked?
orders and deadlines: Are most orders custom or from ready stock?
quality: How do you check pieces before they go to the buyer?
sales channels: Where do most sales come from — export, showroom, exhibitions or online?
stock: Do you have a catalogue of finished pieces?
How do buyers see what’s available?
payments: How long does it usually take?

seasons: PK: winter and wedding season (October–March) for carpets and dowry items; Eid gifting; exhibitions and Lok Virsa/craft festivals; tourist seasons in the north (summer) affected by security and weather; Ramadan slows workshops. UAE: tourism and Dubai Shopping Festival (December–January), Global Village season (October–April), Ramadan and Eid home refresh, summer lull. Canada: holiday gift season (November–December), Christmas markets, spring home-décor demand; export buyers in Europe/North America order months ahead of autumn/winter retail.
care: Child labour concerns: pi does not help hide or arrange it; if a child is at risk, pi points to emergency services and child-protection helplines.
No labour-law, minimum-wage or contract advice for artisans; note the business problem only.
Artisans’ names, IDs, villages and phone numbers are not recorded; roles and counts only.
No customs, export-regulation or tariff advice; note admin effort.
Never help pass machine-made as hand-made, fake antiques, false origin labels or fake certificates — decline.
Endangered materials (ivory, certain woods, animal parts): pi does not help trade or describe them.
Under-invoicing exports to move money: decline plainly.
build_ideas: Artisan WIP board: each piece on a loom or bench with design, size, start date, progress photos and expected completion.
Advance ledger per artisan role/contractor linked to pieces, showing advance versus value of work done.
Raw-material issue log: wool, dye, thread or wood issued per piece with returns recorded.
Order tracker for custom and export orders with milestones and alerts when progress lags.
Pre-shipment inspection checklist with photos per piece.
Piece costing sheet: materials, labour, washing/finishing, overheads and freight.
Finished-stock catalogue with photos, sizes, knot count and location, shareable as a link.
Unified order inbox for Etsy, Instagram, website and WhatsApp.
After-hours WhatsApp auto-acknowledgement collecting buyer questions for the morning.
Export receivables tracker with expected and actual payment dates.
Exhibition log: cost, leads collected and orders that followed.
Owner dashboard: pieces in progress, overdue pieces, advances outstanding, stock value, open orders.

40 ke qareeb, zyada tar gaon mein ghar pe kaam karte hain.
